name: Corning
description: Corning makes specialty glass, ceramics and optical fiber. Its biggest line is optical fiber, cable and connectivity hardware sold to telecom carriers and, increasingly, to data-centre builders for AI; next are the precision glass substrates inside LCD and OLED screens (it calls itself the largest producer), Gorilla Glass cover glass for phones, ceramic emissions-control substrates for vehicles, lab consumables and polysilicon for solar (Hemlock). Customers are concentrated: two customers make up 45 percent of Life Sciences, three make up 59 percent of Display. From Q1 2026 Corning re-cut its reporting into Optical Communications, Glass Innovations (Display plus Specialty Materials), Automotive and Solar; the lines below are the FY2025 10-K segments.

employees.note: Approximately 67,200 full- and part-time employees in 44 countries (10-K FY2025).

businessLines.name: Optical Communications
businessLines.how: Sells optical fiber, cable and connectivity hardware (connectors, assemblies, closures) to telecom carriers (fiber to the home, 5G, submarine) and to enterprise and hyperscale data-centre customers, mostly as volume product sales; some long-term supply agreements with customer deposits. Two customers are 28 percent of segment sales.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

businessLines.name: Display
businessLines.how: Sells fusion-process glass substrates to a few panel makers for LCD and OLED televisions, monitors and notebooks, priced per area; three customers are 59 percent of segment sales. Segment sales are shown at constant currency (the yen hedge adjustment is large).

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

businessLines.name: Specialty Materials
businessLines.how: Gorilla Glass cover glass sold to phone and device makers (Apple a named collaborator) per device design win, plus semiconductor optics, advanced optics and specialty glass sold as components and materials. Two customers are 43 percent of segment sales.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

businessLines.name: Automotive
businessLines.how: Sells ceramic substrates and particulate filters for emissions control to catalyst makers who supply vehicle and engine makers (tied to vehicle production and emissions rules), plus technical and cover glass for vehicle interiors. Three customers are 61 percent of segment sales.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

businessLines.name: Life Sciences
businessLines.how: Sells lab consumables (plastic vessels, labware, glassware, cell culture media) mostly through distributors to pharma, biotech, labs and universities; repeat consumable purchases. Two customers (distributors) are 45 percent of segment sales.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

businessLines.name: Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses
businessLines.how: Hemlock Semiconductor sells high-purity polysilicon to solar-cell and chip wafer makers, often under long-term contracts; also solar wafers and modules, pharmaceutical glass tubing and vials and early-stage ventures.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income (after tax, R&D and depreciation; constant-currency basis)

brands.name: Corning / Falcon / PYREX / Axygen (Life Sciences brands)
Hemlock Semiconductor Group (HSG)
brands.note: polysilicon; polycrystalline silicon sales $955M in FY2025

whatsNext.text: Reporting re-cut in Q1 2026: Display and Specialty Materials combined as Glass Innovations; Hemlock, solar wafers and modules combined as Solar; Life Sciences moved into an all-other group

Long-term partnership with an unnamed customer to strengthen US manufacturing for AI infrastructure; Corning issued warrants for up to 15 million shares at $180 and a pre-funded warrant for up to 3 million shares
Received a $1.0 billion upfront customer deposit tied to a long-term supply agreement in H1 2026
